# Meet day: KiteSink fitness field guide

Your first competition, in order. Each entry gives the point, the reasoning, what to do, how well supported it is, and its sources.

## Guidance

### Classes, gear lists and drug testing differ between federations

**IPF has 8 classes per sex; USA Powerlifting and the USPA list 12 each; check the one you will enter.**

IPF men's classes run from 59 kg to 120+ kg and women's from 47 kg to 84+ kg, plus a lowest sub-junior and junior class of 53 kg (men) or 43 kg (women). USA Powerlifting has 12 classes per sex (men 52 to 140+ kg, women 44 to 100+ kg). The USPA lists 12 (men 52 to 140.1+ kg, women 44 to 110+ kg). Gear must meet the federation's lists, and testing rules differ.

- Check the class table, then the rulebook, of the federation that runs your meet.

Federation and entry · Beginner · Rulebook · Sources: [IPF 2026b](https://www.powerlifting.sport/fileadmin/ipf/data/rules/technical-rules/english/2026_IPF_Technical_Rulebook__effective_01_March_2026__v3.pdf), [USA Powerlifting 2026](https://www.usapowerlifting.com/technical/), [USPA 2025](https://uspa.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/USPA-Rulebook-March-24th-2025.pdf)

### Three referees show white or red lights, then cards give the reason

**White means good lift and red means no lift; after the lights come up, cards show why a lift was turned down.**

In IPF rules each referee controls a white and a red light, and the lights come on together. A red, blue or yellow card (1, 2, 3) shows the reason for a failure. Common reasons: squat depth, double bounce or not standing erect, stepping and missed commands. Bench: bar not reaching the chest or elbows not low enough, downward movement or no lockout, heaving and missed commands. Deadlift: knees or shoulders not locked, supporting the bar on the thighs, lowering early or losing control.

- Ask your coach to note the card colours so you can fix the cause.

Platform and lights · Beginner · Rulebook · Sources: [IPF 2026b](https://www.powerlifting.sport/fileadmin/ipf/data/rules/technical-rules/english/2026_IPF_Technical_Rulebook__effective_01_March_2026__v3.pdf), [USA Powerlifting 2026](https://www.usapowerlifting.com/technical/)

### You can change an opener once; second attempts and bench or squat thirds are locked

**You submit each next weight within one minute of the lights; after that, changes are tightly limited.**

IPF: one change on the first attempt of each lift, higher or lower, up to three minutes before the first round starts for the first group. Second attempts and third attempts in squat and bench cannot be changed. In the third deadlift round you may change twice unless the bar has been called loaded. Weights are multiples of 2.5 kg (5.5 lb) and rise by at least 2.5 kg. If you miss, you may take that weight again, but only in the next round. USA Powerlifting uses the same structure.

- Give your coach the written plan, the minimum increment, and who submits the card.

Attempts and warm-up · Intermediate · Rulebook · Sources: [IPF 2026b](https://www.powerlifting.sport/fileadmin/ipf/data/rules/technical-rules/english/2026_IPF_Technical_Rulebook__effective_01_March_2026__v3.pdf), [USA Powerlifting 2026](https://www.usapowerlifting.com/technical/)

### Caffeine gave a small strength gain in upper-body lifts

**A meta-analysis of 10 strength studies found a small gain overall, clearer for upper-body strength.**

Caffeine improved strength (standardised mean difference 0.20, 95% CI 0.03 to 0.36) and power. For upper-body strength the effect was 0.21 (95% CI 0.02 to 0.39); for lower-body strength it was 0.15 (95% CI -0.05 to 0.34), not clearly different from zero. Effects differ between people and the evidence in women is thin. Avoid trying it for the first time at a meet.

- Try your planned dose in training before the meet.

Attempts and warm-up · Intermediate · Some support · Sources: [Grgic 2018](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12970-018-0216-0)

### Aim for nine good lifts and a smooth day, not a personal record

**A first meet is practice for the whole day: weigh-in, warm-ups, commands and timing.**

Choose an opener that you could lift easily, take a realistic second and add a third only if the second felt solid. Good first-meet goals are hitting all commands, making nine good lifts and learning the flow of a meet. Records and totals come later. Bring a coach or friend who can read the flight order and keep the attempt plan.

- Set two process goals, such as clean commands and on-time warm-ups.

Attempts and warm-up · Beginner · Coaching practice

### Tested meets use drug testing; untested meets may not

**A federation or meet name tells you which one it is; tested and untested results are kept separate.**

USA Powerlifting competes members who have not used performance-enhancing drugs for 36 months and can test members at any time. The USPA allows meet directors to run tested meets with approval, labels them 'Tested' and keeps results and records separate from untested meets. Which one you choose changes who you compete against and whether records count. This is not advice on medicines; ask a doctor if you take any prescription.

- Check whether a meet is tested before you register.

Federation and entry · Beginner · Rulebook · Sources: [USA Powerlifting 2026](https://www.usapowerlifting.com/technical/), [USPA 2025](https://uspa.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/USPA-Rulebook-March-24th-2025.pdf)

## Common mistakes

### Opening with a weight that is nearly a max

**An opener that is hard to lift risks all three attempts and a total; keep it around 88-92% of a current best single.**

Elite classic lifters opened near 91% of their expected third attempt. A heavy opener burns nerves and energy, and a miss uses one of three tries. First-time lifters often over-pick because the day feels exciting. Pick a weight you could lift for a clean double on a normal day, then build.

- Choose an opener from your best recent single, then drop it a little if unsure.

Attempts and warm-up · Beginner · Coaching practice · Sources: [Travis 2021b](https://doi.org/10.1177/0031512520967608)

### Arriving with gear you never checked against the rulebook

**Gear that is not on the list, is too long or too thick, or is torn gets rejected at the equipment check.**

IPF inspectors reject unclean or torn items and gear outside the stated limits, such as a belt over 10 cm (3.9 in) wide or sleeves over 7 mm thick. An item found illegal on the platform after inspection can lead to disqualification. USA Powerlifting requires an equipment check for every competitor. Hats are not allowed on the platform in IPF rules.

- Compare every item with the rulebook two weeks before the meet.

Classes and equipment · Beginner · Rulebook · Sources: [IPF 2026b](https://www.powerlifting.sport/fileadmin/ipf/data/rules/technical-rules/english/2026_IPF_Technical_Rulebook__effective_01_March_2026__v3.pdf), [USA Powerlifting 2026](https://www.usapowerlifting.com/technical/)

### Missing your call because the warm-up ran long

**You have one minute to start your attempt after the bar is called ready; a late start forfeits it.**

IPF: the lifter has one minute from the speaker's call to start the attempt, or the attempt is forfeited. Warm-ups that start too early leave you cold and bored; too late and you walk to the platform rushed. Count lifters ahead of you, use the board, and ask staff when unsure.

- Finish the last warm-up several lifters before your opener.
- Check rack height before you are called.

Attempts and warm-up · Intermediate · Coaching practice · Sources: [IPF 2026b](https://www.powerlifting.sport/fileadmin/ipf/data/rules/technical-rules/english/2026_IPF_Technical_Rulebook__effective_01_March_2026__v3.pdf)

### Trying new food or a big meal after weigh-in

**A large or unfamiliar meal after weigh-in can leave you full or ill when the first squat comes.**

Familiar food is the safe choice. A review of 49 carbohydrate studies found no clear acute strength gain from extra carbohydrate in most cases, so there is little reason to experiment on the day. Eat what has worked on a heavy training day, and keep portions moderate.

- Rehearse your meet-day meals on a heavy training day.

Weigh-in and food · Beginner · Coaching practice · Sources: [Henselmans 2022](https://doi.org/10.3390/nu14040856)

## In order

### Choose a federation: tested or untested sets who you lift against

**Tested federations drug test lifters; untested ones do not. The federation also sets your rules, classes and gear list.**

USA Powerlifting limits competition to members who have not used performance-enhancing drugs for 36 months before the meet, and members can be tested at any time. The USPA offers tested meets only with national office approval, labels them 'Tested' and keeps their results separate from untested meets. IPF coaches in the warm-up and lifting area must acknowledge the IPF Anti-Doping Rules. Classes and gear lists differ, so read the rulebook of the federation you enter.

- Find the federation's meet calendar and read its current rulebook before you enter.

Months out · Beginner · Rulebook · Sources: [IPF 2026b](https://www.powerlifting.sport/fileadmin/ipf/data/rules/technical-rules/english/2026_IPF_Technical_Rulebook__effective_01_March_2026__v3.pdf), [USA Powerlifting 2026](https://www.usapowerlifting.com/technical/), [USPA 2025](https://uspa.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/USPA-Rulebook-March-24th-2025.pdf)

### Register, then pick a class you can reach by normal eating

**Join the federation, enter the meet by its deadline and choose a class near your normal weight.**

USA Powerlifting memberships run from January 1 to December 31. USPA membership covers 12 months from the date of issue. Meets set their own entry forms, fees and deadlines. USPA requires ID and your membership card at weigh-in, and IPF weigh-in requires ID or a passport. Class limits differ between federations (see the class table), so check the one used by your meet.

- Read the meet's entry form for deadlines, fees and the weigh-in schedule.
- Choose the class you can hold with normal eating, not a cut.

Months out · Beginner · Rulebook · Sources: [USA Powerlifting 2026](https://www.usapowerlifting.com/technical/), [USPA 2025](https://uspa.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/USPA-Rulebook-March-24th-2025.pdf), [IPF 2026b](https://www.powerlifting.sport/fileadmin/ipf/data/rules/technical-rules/english/2026_IPF_Technical_Rulebook__effective_01_March_2026__v3.pdf)

### Buy legal gear early and train in it

**In IPF rules you need a singlet, a T-shirt under it, shoes and shin-length socks for the deadlift; belt, sleeves and wraps are optional.**

IPF limits: belt up to 10 cm (3.9 in) wide and 13 mm (0.5 in) thick; knee sleeves up to 7 mm thick and 30 cm (11.8 in) long; wrist wraps up to 1 m (39 in) long and 8 cm (3.1 in) wide; shoe soles up to 5 cm (2 in). Hats are not allowed. Belts, singlets and sleeves must come from makers on the IPF Approved List. USA Powerlifting uses the same sleeve and wrist wrap limits. Wear all of it in the last heavy sessions.

- Check each item against your federation's approved list before you buy it.
- Wear the full kit for your last heavy sessions.

Weeks out · Beginner · Rulebook · Sources: [IPF 2026b](https://www.powerlifting.sport/fileadmin/ipf/data/rules/technical-rules/english/2026_IPF_Technical_Rulebook__effective_01_March_2026__v3.pdf), [USA Powerlifting 2026](https://www.usapowerlifting.com/technical/), [Grgic 2017](https://doi.org/10.1519/JSC.0000000000001699)

### Plan nine attempts with your coach or a trusted friend

**Plan an opener you could lift easily on any day, a realistic second, and a hard but makeable third.**

Elite classic lifters at IPF World Championships opened near 91% of their expected third attempt, then added about 5% for the second and about 3% for the third. Across 10,672 raw entries in Australian meets, squat openers averaged 92% of the lifter's best squat that day. Base your plan on your best recent single, not on a hope. Write all nine weights down with a lighter plan B for each lift, and round to 2.5 kg (5.5 lb) steps.

- Use the attempt table below, and your best recent single, to fill in all nine weights.

Weeks out · Beginner · Coaching practice · Sources: [Travis 2021b](https://doi.org/10.1177/0031512520967608), [Howells 2022](https://doi.org/10.23736/S0022-4707.21.12140-1)

### Taper over the last week or two: less volume, a few heavy singles

**Survey data show a step taper with 41-50% less volume, the last heavy squat and deadlift 7-10 days out, and rest in the last days.**

In 364 North American raw powerlifters, a step taper over 7 to 10 days with 41-50% less volume was typical. The last heavy squat and deadlift came 7 to 10 days out, the last heavy bench under 7 days out, and full rest about 2.8 days before the meet. In a small trial of 19 athletes, 3 days off kept upper- and lower-body strength; 5 days off cost upper-body strength. A review found limited evidence that a short, heavy, low-volume session within 48 hours of competition can help.

- Keep the lifts, cut the sets, and stop hard training about 3 days out.

The week before · Intermediate · Thin evidence · Sources: [Travis 2021a](https://doi.org/10.1519/JSC.0000000000004177), [Travis 2022](https://doi.org/10.1519/JSC.0000000000004183), [Harrison 2019](https://doi.org/10.1007/s40279-019-01136-3)

### Confirm the schedule, travel and food for the meet

**Know your session, weigh-in time and flight, and have travel and meals sorted before the last days.**

Find your session and flight on the meet schedule and confirm with the meet director. Book a bed close to the venue if the drive is long. Plan your food for the day before and the day of the meet, and pack the bag early. Squat and bench rack heights are written down at weigh-in, so measure yours in training.

- Pack the bag a few days early using the checklist below.
- Note your squat and bench rack heights and foot-block settings.

The week before · Beginner · Coaching practice

### Lay out gear, eat familiar food and sleep as normally as you can

**Eat meals that you know sit well, drink fluids steadily and avoid new foods or heavy training.**

Lay out singlet, T-shirt, socks, belt, shoes and ID. Skip new foods and alcohol. A poor night before a meet is common and a single night with little sleep had little effect on muscle strength in a systematic review of 17 studies, while several nights of restricted sleep could reduce force in compound lifts. Go to bed at your usual time and do not worry about one bad night.

- Keep the day light: a short walk and easy mobility at most.
- Go to bed at your normal time.

The day before · Beginner · Coaching practice · Sources: [Knowles 2018](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jsams.2018.01.012)

### Weigh in about two hours before lifting, with ID and your opening attempts

**IPF and USA Powerlifting weigh-ins run for 90 minutes and start two hours before lifting; the USPA can offer one up to 24 hours before.**

IPF: weigh-in no earlier than two hours before the start for a category and lasts one and a half hours; bring ID or a passport; opening attempts are declared at weigh-in. USA Powerlifting: weigh-in starts two hours before lifting, lasts 90 minutes and ends 30 minutes before lifting. USPA: weigh-in lasts at least 90 minutes, with an optional early weigh-in up to 24 hours before lifting. If you miss class weight, you may return to the scale within the window.

- Arrive early, bring ID and your written openers, and keep your gear bag with you.

Weigh-in · Beginner · Rulebook · Sources: [IPF 2026b](https://www.powerlifting.sport/fileadmin/ipf/data/rules/technical-rules/english/2026_IPF_Technical_Rulebook__effective_01_March_2026__v3.pdf), [USA Powerlifting 2026](https://www.usapowerlifting.com/technical/), [USPA 2025](https://uspa.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/USPA-Rulebook-March-24th-2025.pdf)

### Pass the equipment check and sign the rack height sheet

**Referees inspect and approve each item you plan to wear; an illegal item found later can disqualify you.**

IPF: at least two referees inspect gear any time up to 30 minutes before your category starts; unclean or torn items are rejected, and over-length wraps can be cut and resubmitted. If you appear on the platform with an illegal item, you are disqualified. USA Powerlifting: every competitor has an equipment check, normally during the weigh-in period, with a 30-minute deadline before the session. Check squat and bench rack heights and sign the sheet.

- Bring every item you plan to wear, including your belt and sleeves.
- Sign the rack height sheet after checking each height.

Weigh-in · Beginner · Rulebook · Sources: [IPF 2026b](https://www.powerlifting.sport/fileadmin/ipf/data/rules/technical-rules/english/2026_IPF_Technical_Rulebook__effective_01_March_2026__v3.pdf), [USA Powerlifting 2026](https://www.usapowerlifting.com/technical/)

### Eat and drink steadily after weigh-in, using food you know

**After weigh-in, eat a familiar meal and sip fluids, then keep snacks nearby for the rest of the day.**

Eat normal, familiar foods and avoid very large or high-fibre meals just before the first squat. A systematic review of 49 carbohydrate studies found extra carbohydrate did not improve acute performance in 13 studies, and helped in six, mainly in fasted lifters or workouts of more than 10 sets per muscle group. A meet day is long, so steady eating and drinking matters more than any single food.

- Eat a normal meal within an hour of weigh-in.
- Sip fluids across the morning instead of drinking a large amount at once.

Weigh-in · Beginner · Thin evidence · Sources: [Henselmans 2022](https://doi.org/10.3390/nu14040856)

### Time your warm-up from the flight order, not the clock

**Work backwards from your opener: count the lifters ahead of you and finish your last warm-up a few lifters before your call.**

Check the board for the flight order and watch how fast the platform moves. A common plan is a general warm-up, then 4 to 6 ramping sets on the bar, with the last warm-up about three to four lifters before your opener. Under IPF rules a single group gets 20 minutes between lifts, and each lifter has one minute to start after being called. Ask a coach or loader if you are unsure how many lifters are left.

- Ask the warm-up room staff how many lifters are ahead of you every few minutes.
- Be ready at the platform area when the lifter before you takes the bar.

The warm-up room · Intermediate · Coaching practice · Sources: [IPF 2026b](https://www.powerlifting.sport/fileadmin/ipf/data/rules/technical-rules/english/2026_IPF_Technical_Rulebook__effective_01_March_2026__v3.pdf)

### Squat: wait for the command, reach depth, wait for 'rack'

**After unracking, stand still with knees locked and wait for 'Squat'; squat below parallel, stand up, then wait for 'Rack'.**

IPF: step back, stand motionless with knees locked, and wait for the downward arm movement and 'Squat'. The top of the legs at the hip joint must go lower than the top of the knees, in one descent, then you rise with knees locked and wait for 'Rack'. If you are not in position after five seconds you hear 'Replace'. USA Powerlifting and the USPA use the same words. Foot movement, double bounces and missing a command can turn the lift down.

- Settle, take a breath and wait for the full command before you move.

On the platform · Beginner · Rulebook · Sources: [IPF 2026b](https://www.powerlifting.sport/fileadmin/ipf/data/rules/technical-rules/english/2026_IPF_Technical_Rulebook__effective_01_March_2026__v3.pdf), [USA Powerlifting 2026](https://www.usapowerlifting.com/technical/), [USPA 2025](https://uspa.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/USPA-Rulebook-March-24th-2025.pdf)

### Bench: wait for 'start', pause on the chest, wait for 'press'

**Lock the elbows and wait for 'Start'; lower the bar to your chest, hold still, wait for 'Press', then press and wait for 'Rack'.**

IPF: head, shoulders and buttocks stay on the bench and feet stay flat on the floor. Grip with thumbs around the bar and hands no wider than 81 cm (32 in) between the forefingers. After 'Start', the bar goes to the chest or abdominal area and the underside of the elbows reaches level with or below the shoulders. Hold motionless until 'Press', then lock the arms and wait for 'Rack'. USA Powerlifting and the USPA use the same words.

- Practise the pause on every training rep, with a count you can repeat.

On the platform · Beginner · Rulebook · Sources: [IPF 2026b](https://www.powerlifting.sport/fileadmin/ipf/data/rules/technical-rules/english/2026_IPF_Technical_Rulebook__effective_01_March_2026__v3.pdf), [USA Powerlifting 2026](https://www.usapowerlifting.com/technical/), [USPA 2025](https://uspa.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/USPA-Rulebook-March-24th-2025.pdf)

### Deadlift: pull to a full lockout and wait for 'down'

**Stand erect with knees locked and shoulders back and wait for 'Down'; then lower the bar with control.**

IPF, USA Powerlifting and USPA use one command, 'Down', given once the bar is held motionless at a full lockout. Reasons for a turn-down include downward movement of the bar before lockout, supporting the bar on the thighs, lowering it before the command, losing control with both hands, and stepping. Foot movement after the command is not a fault. In IPF and USA Powerlifting meets you may change a third-attempt deadlift twice, unless you were already called to a bar loaded to your submitted weight.

- Stand tall, hold the lockout for a beat, and wait for the command.

On the platform · Beginner · Rulebook · Sources: [IPF 2026b](https://www.powerlifting.sport/fileadmin/ipf/data/rules/technical-rules/english/2026_IPF_Technical_Rulebook__effective_01_March_2026__v3.pdf), [USA Powerlifting 2026](https://www.usapowerlifting.com/technical/), [USPA 2025](https://uspa.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/USPA-Rulebook-March-24th-2025.pdf)

### Between flights: small snacks, fluids, and caffeine only if tried

**Eat and drink in small amounts between lifts and try any caffeine in training first.**

A meta-analysis of 10 strength studies found caffeine gave a small strength gain overall (standardised mean difference 0.20, 95% CI 0.03 to 0.36), clearer for the upper body than the lower body. Keep snacks small and familiar, and keep fluid steady. Caffeine affects people differently, so use only what you have used in training and stop if it causes jitters or an upset stomach.

- Eat a small familiar snack and sip fluid after each discipline.
- Use caffeine only in amounts you have tried in training.

Between lifts · Beginner · Some support · Sources: [Grgic 2018](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12970-018-0216-0)

### After the meet: results, food, rest and a review

**Collect your results, eat and rest, and review what the attempts taught you before you plan the next cycle.**

Ask for the score sheet and any video, and note which attempts were turned down and the reason shown on the cards. Eat and drink normally and take a few easy days before hard training starts. In tested federations you can be asked for a sample after lifting; follow the doping control officer's instructions. Write down what you would change about openers, warm-ups and food for the next meet.

- Write a short review the next day, while details are fresh.

Afterwards · Beginner · Coaching practice

## Key numbers

| Number | What it is | Support | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|
| 88-92 % of best single | Opener as a share of your current best single: A conservative first attempt; elite classic lifters opened near 91% of their expected third attempt. | Coaching practice | [Travis 2021b](https://doi.org/10.1177/0031512520967608) |
| 94-97.5 % of best single | Second attempt as a share of your current best single: A step up from the opener of about 5% for elite classic lifters; a realistic, solid weight. | Coaching practice | [Travis 2021b](https://doi.org/10.1177/0031512520967608) |
| 98-102.5 % of best single | Third attempt as a share of your current best single: An aim around your best single, up to a small personal best if the day feels good. | Coaching practice | [Travis 2021b](https://doi.org/10.1177/0031512520967608) |
| 2 hours before lifting | Weigh-in start before lifting: IPF: no earlier than two hours before the category starts. USA Powerlifting: weigh-in starts two hours before lifting. | Rulebook | [IPF 2026b](https://www.powerlifting.sport/fileadmin/ipf/data/rules/technical-rules/english/2026_IPF_Technical_Rulebook__effective_01_March_2026__v3.pdf), [USA Powerlifting 2026](https://www.usapowerlifting.com/technical/) |
| 90 minutes | Length of the weigh-in period: IPF: one and a half hours. USA Powerlifting: 90 minutes, ending 30 minutes before lifting. USPA: at least 90 minutes. | Rulebook | [IPF 2026b](https://www.powerlifting.sport/fileadmin/ipf/data/rules/technical-rules/english/2026_IPF_Technical_Rulebook__effective_01_March_2026__v3.pdf), [USA Powerlifting 2026](https://www.usapowerlifting.com/technical/), [USPA 2025](https://uspa.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/USPA-Rulebook-March-24th-2025.pdf) |
| 1 minute | Time to start an attempt after being called: IPF: one minute from the speaker's call to the start of the attempt; USPA also gives one minute. | Rulebook | [IPF 2026b](https://www.powerlifting.sport/fileadmin/ipf/data/rules/technical-rules/english/2026_IPF_Technical_Rulebook__effective_01_March_2026__v3.pdf), [USPA 2025](https://uspa.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/USPA-Rulebook-March-24th-2025.pdf) |
| 2.5 kg (5.5 lb) | Minimum step between attempts: IPF weights are multiples of 2.5 kg, rising at least 2.5 kg between attempts; a missed weight can be repeated. USA Powerlifting uses 2.5 kg increments. | Rulebook | [IPF 2026b](https://www.powerlifting.sport/fileadmin/ipf/data/rules/technical-rules/english/2026_IPF_Technical_Rulebook__effective_01_March_2026__v3.pdf), [USA Powerlifting 2026](https://www.usapowerlifting.com/technical/) |
| 30 seconds | Time to leave the platform after an attempt: IPF and USA Powerlifting: leave the platform within 30 seconds of the end of an attempt. | Rulebook | [IPF 2026b](https://www.powerlifting.sport/fileadmin/ipf/data/rules/technical-rules/english/2026_IPF_Technical_Rulebook__effective_01_March_2026__v3.pdf), [USA Powerlifting 2026](https://www.usapowerlifting.com/technical/) |

IPF classes from the 2026 Technical Rules Book; pounds are converted from the kilogram limits.

| Men (kg) | Men upper limit (lb) | Women (kg) | Women upper limit (lb) |
|---|---|---|---|

| 74.0 kg: 66.01 to 74.0 kg | up to 163.1 lb | 57.0 kg: 52.01 to 57.0 kg | up to 125.7 lb |

Rulebook · Sources: [IPF 2026b](https://www.powerlifting.sport/fileadmin/ipf/data/rules/technical-rules/english/2026_IPF_Technical_Rulebook__effective_01_March_2026__v3.pdf)

## Platform commands for each lift

Commands as given by the chief referee in IPF, USA Powerlifting and USPA rules; wait for each one.

| Lift | Commands in order | What you do first | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Squat | 'Squat', then 'Rack' | Stand erect, knees locked, motionless | Depth: top of legs at the hip below the top of the knees |
| Bench press | 'Start', 'Press', 'Rack' | Arms locked and still for 'Start'; bar still on chest for 'Press' | Elbows level with or below the shoulders at the chest |
| Deadlift | 'Down' | Stand erect, knees locked, shoulders back | One command, given once the lockout is held |
| Squat or bench | 'Replace' | Fix the reason the referee gives you | IPF: if not in position after five seconds |

Rulebook · Sources: [IPF 2026b](https://www.powerlifting.sport/fileadmin/ipf/data/rules/technical-rules/english/2026_IPF_Technical_Rulebook__effective_01_March_2026__v3.pdf), [USA Powerlifting 2026](https://www.usapowerlifting.com/technical/), [USPA 2025](https://uspa.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/USPA-Rulebook-March-24th-2025.pdf)

## Attempt selection ranges from competition data

Typical ranges as a share of a current best single, with an example at 200 kg (441 lb). They follow elite and national meet data; no study covers first meets.

| Attempt | % of current best single | Example at 200 kg (441 lb) | Aim |
|---|---|---|---|
| Opener | 88-92% | 176-184 kg (388-406 lb) | A weight you could lift easily on any day |
| Second | 94-97.5% | 188-195 kg (414-430 lb) | A solid, realistic lift |
| Third | 98-102.5% | 196-205 kg (432-452 lb) | A hard but makeable attempt |

Coaching practice · Sources: [Travis 2021b](https://doi.org/10.1177/0031512520967608), [Howells 2022](https://doi.org/10.23736/S0022-4707.21.12140-1)

## Meet bag checklist

Pack in the days before the meet, and check the rules of your federation for each item.

**Required to lift**

- Singlet
- T-shirt to wear under the singlet
- Shin-length socks for the deadlift
- Lifting shoes or deadlift slippers
- Photo ID or passport
- Federation membership card

**Optional gear (if your federation allows)**

- Belt (IPF: up to 10 cm / 3.9 in wide, 13 mm thick)
- Knee sleeves (up to 7 mm thick, 30 cm / 11.8 in long)
- Wrist wraps (up to 1 m / 39 in long, 8 cm / 3.1 in wide)
- Chalk or baby powder, if the meet allows it
- Medical tape for thumbs (IPF: two layers at most)

**Paperwork and plan**

- Entry confirmation and the meet schedule
- Written plan for all nine attempts
- Squat and bench rack heights and foot-block settings
- Pen and notebook

**Food and drink**

- Familiar meal for after weigh-in
- Small snacks for between flights
- Water or a drink you have used in training
- Caffeine only if you have tried it in training

**Comfort and recovery**

- Spare T-shirt and socks
- Towel
- Warm layer for the warm-up room
- Phone charger
- A friend or coach to hand up attempt cards

## Terms

- **Bomb out**: To miss all three attempts on a lift; in a full-power meet that usually means no total.
- **Chief referee**: The referee who gives the commands on the platform; two side referees also judge each lift.
- **Classic (raw)**: A division with a non-supportive singlet and no supportive suits, shirts or knee wraps; belt, knee sleeves and wrist wraps are allowed within limits.
- **Flight (group)**: A group of lifters who take their attempts together; larger sessions split into flights, with lower previous totals lifting first in IPF rules.
- **Lot number**: A number drawn at weigh-in; if two lifters choose the same weight, the lower lot number lifts first.
- **Opener (first attempt)**: The first of your three attempts on a lift; chosen to be easy enough that you lift it with room to spare.
- **Rack height sheet**: The form where you record squat and bench rack and foot-block settings at weigh-in, so loaders set them before your attempt.
- **Spotter/loaders**: Helpers who load the bar and spot squat and bench; two to five are on the platform at a time in IPF rules.

# Nutrition: KiteSink fitness field guide

Eating to support training, and tracking it honestly. Each entry gives the point, the reasoning, what to do, how well supported it is, and its sources.

## Guidance

### Body weight follows energy balance, but it moves slowly

**Eat above what you burn and weight rises, eat below and it falls, but the change takes months to show its full size.**

A mathematical model of adult metabolism found that body weight responds slowly to a change in intake, with a half time of about one year. It also estimated that a persistent gap of only about 30 kJ (7 kcal) a day lies behind the average weight gain seen in the US. In a ward study of 20 adults, weight change tracked energy intake closely (r = 0.8). Small daily gaps add up, and a single day rarely shows.

- Judge a calorie target over weeks, not days.

Energy and maintenance · Beginner · Some support · Sources: [Hall 2011](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(11)60812-X), [Hall 2019](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cmet.2019.05.008)

### Calorie calculators give a starting point, not your maintenance

**Even the best resting-rate equation is within 10 percent of measured for most people, and many individuals fall outside it.**

A systematic review compared four equations for resting metabolic rate. Mifflin-St Jeor predicted within 10 percent of the measured value for more people than the others, and it still missed for a share of individuals. Total daily need is that resting figure multiplied by an activity level, and the FAO/WHO/UNU report gives about 1.40 to 2.40 as the range sustained by free-living adults. A wide range of activity levels means a wide range of totals.

- Eat your estimate for two to three weeks while weighing yourself daily.
- Adjust by 100 to 200 kcal if weight moves the wrong way.

Energy and maintenance · Beginner · Well supported · Sources: [Frankenfield 2005](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jada.2005.02.005), [FAO/WHO/UNU 2004](https://www.fao.org/4/y5686e/y5686e07.htm)

### Most lifters do well on 1.6 to 2.2 g of protein per kg a day

**About 1.6 to 2.2 g per kg (0.7 to 1.0 g per lb) of body weight a day covers most people who lift to build muscle.**

The ISSN position stand calls 1.4 to 2.0 g/kg a day sufficient for most exercising people. A meta-analysis of 74 trials found added protein helped lean mass in adults under 65 who ate 1.6 g/kg or more. A dose-response review of 105 trials (5,402 participants) found each extra 0.1 g/kg added 0.39 kg of lean mass below 1.3 g/kg a day and 0.12 kg above it. Returns shrink as intake rises.

- Set a daily target in grams from your body weight, then check it weekly.
- Take the lower half of the range if food budget is tight.

Protein · Beginner · Well supported · Sources: [Jäger 2017](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12970-017-0177-8), [Nunes 2022b](https://doi.org/10.1002/jcsm.12922), [Tagawa 2021](https://doi.org/10.1093/nutrit/nuaa104), [Iraki 2019](https://doi.org/10.3390/sports7070154)

### High protein does not harm kidney function in healthy adults

**In healthy adults without kidney disease, higher protein intakes did not reduce kidney filtration in trials.**

A meta-analysis pooled 28 trials with 1,358 participants who ate 1.5 g/kg a day or more, or at least 20 percent of energy, against lower intakes. Filtration rate was slightly higher after high-protein eating, and the change from baseline did not differ between groups. The trials were short and had some risk of selection bias. This does not cover people who already have kidney disease. They should ask their clinician.

- If you have kidney disease or a family history, check your protein plan with a clinician first.

Protein · Beginner · Well supported · Sources: [Devries 2018](https://doi.org/10.1093/jn/nxy197)

### Spread protein over several meals, but the split matters less than the total

**About 0.25 to 0.55 g per kg per meal is a sound target (20 to 40 g for most people), and the daily total is what matters most.**

The ISSN stand suggests 0.25 g/kg or 20 to 40 g per serving, spread across the day. A bodybuilding review pairs 1.6 to 2.2 g/kg a day with 0.40 to 0.55 g/kg per meal over 3 to 6 meals. Muscle protein synthesis levelled off at about 0.24 g/kg in younger men and 0.40 g/kg in older men. In eight adults, even meals raised 24-hour synthesis 25 percent more than a skewed pattern. A review calls the distribution evidence limited and inconsistent, and a tracer study found 100 g produced a larger, longer response than 25 g, so there is no hard cap per meal.

- Aim for three to five protein-containing meals.
- Do not worry about one bigger protein meal.

Protein · Intermediate · Some support · Sources: [Jäger 2017](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12970-017-0177-8), [Moore 2015](https://doi.org/10.1093/gerona/glu103), [Mamerow 2014](https://doi.org/10.3945/jn.113.185280), [Hudson 2020](https://doi.org/10.3390/nu12051441), [Trommelen 2023](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.xcrm.2023.101324), [Iraki 2019](https://doi.org/10.3390/sports7070154)

### Protein timing around training matters little next to the daily total

**Eating protein straight after training is fine, but a precise window does not change results once daily intake is met.**

A systematic review of 65 studies with 2,907 participants found protein supplementation raised lean body mass in adults and older adults, and subgroup analyses showed no benefit from any specific timing. The ISSN position says the anabolic effect of exercise lasts at least 24 hours. A protein-containing meal before or after training is a reasonable habit, and it is not urgent.

- Eat a protein meal within a few hours either side of training.

Timing, fluids and alcohol · Beginner · Well supported · Sources: [Wirth 2020](https://doi.org/10.1093/jn/nxaa049), [Jäger 2017](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12970-017-0177-8)

### Plant protein builds muscle about as well, given enough total protein

**When total protein is adequate, plant and animal sources give similar muscle and strength gains over months.**

A meta-analysis of 18 studies found protein source did not change absolute lean mass or strength, though animal protein favoured percent lean mass, and younger adults gained 0.41 kg more lean mass with animal protein. In a 12-week trial, 19 vegans and 19 omnivores on 1.6 g/kg gained muscle alike. A soy-versus-animal meta-analysis of nine studies agreed. Single-meal studies do show a lower response to soy and wheat, which is why total intake matters.

- If you eat no animal foods, aim for the upper half of the protein range.
- Mix soy, legumes and grains across the day.

Protein · Intermediate · Well supported · Sources: [Lim 2021](https://doi.org/10.3390/nu13020661), [Hevia-Larraín 2021](https://doi.org/10.1007/s40279-021-01434-9), [Messina 2018](https://doi.org/10.1123/ijsnem.2018-0071), [van Vliet 2015](https://doi.org/10.3945/jn.114.204305)

### Carbohydrate boosts lifting only in long, high-volume sessions

**Carbohydrate intake had little effect on strength training in short fed sessions, and may help when volume is high.**

A systematic review of 49 studies found that carbohydrate intake per se is unlikely to change strength training performance in a fed state in workouts of up to 10 sets per muscle group. Acute gains showed up mostly in fasted comparisons and higher volumes. For long or very hard sessions, a sports nutrition review gives 30 to 60 g an hour during sessions of more than an hour. Physique-athlete reviews suggest at least 3 to 5 g/kg a day.

- After protein and fat are set, fill the rest of your calories with carbohydrate you enjoy.

Carbs, fat and fibre · Intermediate · Some support · Sources: [Henselmans 2022](https://doi.org/10.3390/nu14040856), [Burke 2011a](https://doi.org/10.1080/02640414.2011.585473), [Iraki 2019](https://doi.org/10.3390/sports7070154)

### Keep fat from falling too low: about 15 to 30 percent of calories

**Fat of roughly 0.5 to 1.5 g per kg, or 15 to 30 percent of energy, is a sound band, and very low fat has costs.**

Reviews for lean physique athletes suggest 15 to 30 percent of calories from fat, or 0.5 to 1.5 g/kg in the off-season, with a low end of 10 to 25 percent in contest preparation. A meta-analysis of six trials (206 men) found low-fat diets lowered total testosterone (standardised difference -0.38) against high-fat diets. This is mainly a floor for hormones and diet quality, not a target to push higher.

- Do not cut fat below about 0.5 g per kg of body weight for long.

Carbs, fat and fibre · Intermediate · Some support · Sources: [Iraki 2019](https://doi.org/10.3390/sports7070154), [Helms 2014b](https://doi.org/10.1186/1550-2783-11-20), [Roberts 2020](https://doi.org/10.2478/hukin-2019-0096), [Whittaker 2021](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jsbmb.2021.105878)

### Aim for 25 to 29 g of fibre a day

**In large analyses, health benefits from fibre were greatest at about 25 to 29 g a day, with more possibly better.**

A series of meta-analyses covered 185 prospective studies and 58 trials with 4,635 adults. Observational data suggested 15 to 30 percent lower all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in the highest fibre eaters against the lowest, and trials showed lower body weight, blood pressure and cholesterol with more fibre. Risk reduction was greatest at 25 to 29 g a day. Raise intake gradually and drink fluids with it.

- Add fibre slowly over a few weeks.

Carbs, fat and fibre · Beginner · Well supported · Sources: [Reynolds 2019](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(18)31809-9)

### Pre-workout eating helps in long sessions, and little else about timing is critical

**Daily totals decide results, and a meal before training mostly helps if you train fasted or do high volume.**

The joint position stand of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics, Dietitians of Canada and the ACSM says performance and recovery improve with well-chosen type, amount and timing of food and fluids. In the carbohydrate review, the acute benefits appeared mostly in fasted comparisons and workouts above 10 sets per muscle group. Physique reviews suggest a protein dose of 0.4 to 0.5 g/kg before and after sessions as a convenient pattern.

- Eat a normal meal one to three hours before hard sessions.

Timing, fluids and alcohol · Intermediate · Some support · Sources: [Thomas 2016](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jand.2015.12.006), [Henselmans 2022](https://doi.org/10.3390/nu14040856), [Helms 2014b](https://doi.org/10.1186/1550-2783-11-20)

### Being under-hydrated lowers strength and muscle endurance

**Hypohydration reduced strength by about 5.5 percent and muscle endurance by about 8 percent in a meta-analysis.**

A meta-analysis of 28 papers found hypohydration, meaning a body fluid deficit, cut muscle endurance by 8.3 percent, strength by 5.5 percent and anaerobic power by 5.8 percent. Dehydrating by exercise hurt more than passive methods, and trained people tended to lose less. This is about ordinary fluid habits. Deliberate dehydration to make a weight class is risky and needs an experienced coach and clinician.

- Start sessions well hydrated and drink during long or hot ones.
- Never use extreme dehydration to change weight quickly.

Timing, fluids and alcohol · Beginner · Well supported · Sources: [Savoie 2015](https://doi.org/10.1007/s40279-015-0349-0)

### Heavy drinking after hard training blunts the muscle repair signal

**A very large dose of alcohol after training cut muscle protein synthesis by 24 to 37 percent in one small study.**

Eight active men did a hard session of legs and cycling, then drank alcohol at 1.5 g/kg (about 12 standard drinks) with either protein or carbohydrate. Muscle protein synthesis was 24 percent lower with alcohol and protein, and 37 percent lower with alcohol and carbohydrate, than with protein alone. That is one small study at a heavy dose. Effects of one or two drinks were not tested.

- Keep drinking light on the days you most want to recover.

Timing, fluids and alcohol · Intermediate · Thin evidence · Sources: [Parr 2014](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0088384)

### Alcohol adds calories that people do not offset by eating less

**Across 22 studies, people did not eat less after drinking, so total energy for the day rose.**

A meta-analysis of 22 studies with 701 participants found no compensation for alcoholic energy: food intake rose by 343 kJ (about 82 kcal), and total energy intake rose by 1,072 kJ (about 256 kcal). Alcohol itself provides 7 kcal per gram on the standard Atwater scale, between carbohydrate and fat. Counting drinks in your log is the only way to see this.

- Log drinks like food, and count mixers.

Timing, fluids and alcohol · Beginner · Well supported · Sources: [Kwok 2019](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0007114518003677), [FAO 2003](https://www.fao.org/4/y5022e/y5022e04.htm)

### Creatine monohydrate is the best-supported lifting supplement

**Taking 3 to 5 g of creatine monohydrate a day adds lean mass when combined with training, and it is safe for healthy people.**

A meta-analysis of 35 trials with 1,192 participants found creatine added 1.10 kg of lean mass when combined with resistance training. Men gained 1.46 kg, and women a non-significant 0.29 kg, though women were fewer in the data. The ISSN position stand finds supplementation up to 30 g a day for 5 years safe in healthy people. The 3 to 5 g daily dose comes from a physique-athlete review. In 31 men, 3 g a day raised muscle creatine over 28 days by about as much as 20 g a day did in 6 days.

- Take 3 to 5 g of creatine monohydrate every day.

Supplements · Beginner · Well supported · Sources: [Delpino 2022](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.nut.2022.111791), [Kreider 2017](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12970-017-0173-z), [Iraki 2019](https://doi.org/10.3390/sports7070154), [Hultman 1996](https://doi.org/10.1152/jappl.1996.81.1.232)

### Caffeine gives a small, real boost to strength and power

**In a meta-analysis, caffeine raised maximal strength and power slightly, mostly in the upper body.**

A meta-analysis of 10 studies on strength and 10 on power found caffeine improved both (standardised differences 0.20 and 0.17). The effect was significant for upper-body strength, and not for lower-body. The review also notes poor blinding and little data for women. The ISSN's 2010 stand found about 3 to 6 mg/kg effective, with no further gain at 9 mg/kg or more; a bodybuilding review lists 5 to 6 mg/kg.

- Test your dose in training before a key session.

Supplements · Beginner · Well supported · Sources: [Grgic 2018](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12970-018-0216-0), [Iraki 2019](https://doi.org/10.3390/sports7070154), [Goldstein 2010](https://doi.org/10.1186/1550-2783-7-5)

### Beta-alanine and citrulline help in specific cases, with modest effects

**Beta-alanine helps efforts of one to four minutes, and citrulline malate added about three reps per exercise.**

The ISSN stand says 4 to 6 g of beta-alanine daily for two to four weeks improves exercise performance, most clearly in tasks lasting 1 to 4 minutes, and tingling, the main side effect, is reduced by splitting the dose into amounts of about 1.6 g. A meta-analysis of eight studies (137 participants) found 6 to 8 g of citrulline malate taken 40 to 60 minutes before lifting added about 3 repetitions (6.4 percent). Both effects are small next to training and sleep.

- Consider these only after protein, creatine and training are in place.

Supplements · Intermediate · Some support · Sources: [Trexler 2015](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12970-015-0090-y), [Vårvik 2021](https://doi.org/10.1123/ijsnem.2020-0295)

### Most supplements lack good evidence, and some carry risks

**The IOC finds only a few supplements, including caffeine and creatine, have good evidence, and the rest are unproven.**

The IOC consensus says nutrition makes a small but valuable contribution and few supplements have good evidence of benefit; some risk contamination with banned substances. BCAA pills have no human studies of oral BCAA alone on muscle synthesis. A review of 50 testosterone-booster products found no testosterone data for 61.5 percent of them, and data showing a rise for 24.8 percent.

- Buy from brands with third-party testing if you compete in a tested sport.

Supplements · Beginner · Some support · Sources: [Maughan 2018](https://doi.org/10.1136/bjsports-2018-099027), [Wolfe 2017](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12970-017-0184-9), [Clemesha 2020](https://doi.org/10.5534/wjmh.190043)

### Logging food is linked to better results, and frequency matters most

**People who logged more often lost more, and a rough log kept consistently beats a perfect one kept rarely.**

A systematic review of 22 studies found a significant association between self-monitoring and weight loss, though the evidence was weak because of method limits. In a 24-week program of 142 people, those losing 5 percent or more of their weight logged in 2.4 times a day against 1.6 for the rest, and time per day fell from about 23 to 15 minutes. These are observational links, not proof logging causes the loss.

- Log at the time you eat, and aim for most days, not perfect days.

Tracking food · Beginner · Some support · Sources: [Burke 2011b](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jada.2010.10.008), [Harvey 2019](https://doi.org/10.1002/oby.22382)

### US labels may legally run up to 20 percent above the declared calories

**A US food is misbranded only if its calories exceed the declared value by more than 20 percent.**

Under 21 CFR 101.9(g)(5), a food is deemed misbranded if the measured calories, sugars, fat, saturated fat, trans fat, cholesterol or sodium exceed the label by more than 20 percent. Measured snack foods did better than that: in 24 products the median was 4.3 percent above the label, in the legal range. Other countries have their own tolerances, so check yours. Treat any label as an estimate.

- Expect small errors, and weigh food rather than trust serving counts.

Tracking food · Beginner · Rulebook · Sources: [UFDA 2023](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2023-title21-vol2/xml/CFR-2023-title21-vol2-sec101-9.xml), [Jumpertz 2013](https://doi.org/10.1002/oby.20185)

### Under-reporting is the norm, even among athletes and dietitians

**Self-reported intake is usually below true intake, by around a fifth in athletes and by more in some groups.**

A systematic review of 59 studies of 6,298 adults, using doubly labeled water as the reference, found most reported significant under-reporting. In athletes, intake was 19 percent too low on average. In 20 women, dietitians under-reported by 223 kcal a day and controls by 429. Ten people who said they could not lose weight on under 1,200 kcal actually under-reported by 47 percent, a small group.

- If weight is not changing, assume your log is low before blaming metabolism.

Tracking food · Beginner · Well supported · Sources: [Burrows 2019](https://doi.org/10.3389/fendo.2019.00850), [Capling 2017](https://doi.org/10.3390/nu9121313), [CHAMPAGNE 2002](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0002-8223(02)90316-0), [Lichtman 1992](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJM199212313272701)

### Tracking can feed disordered eating in people who are prone to it

**Calorie apps are linked to more eating-disorder symptoms in surveys, and many patients blame them.**

Among 105 people diagnosed with an eating disorder, about 75 percent used My Fitness Pal and 73 percent of those said it contributed to their illness. In 122 men, app users had higher eating-disorder symptoms than non-users, and 493 students showed the same link. These are cross-sectional surveys, so the app may attract people already at risk. Take the signal seriously either way.

- Stop tracking and talk to a clinician if logging brings guilt, fear or rules you cannot break.

Tracking food · Intermediate · Thin evidence · Sources: [Levinson 2017](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eatbeh.2017.08.003), [Linardon 2019](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eatbeh.2019.02.003), [Simpson 2017](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eatbeh.2017.02.002)

### Hand portions are a rougher but gentler way to estimate food

**Using your hand as a ruler reached within 25 percent of the true weight for most simple foods in one study.**

In 67 adults who estimated 42 pre-weighed foods, a finger-width method put 80 percent of geometric foods within 25 percent of true weight and 13 percent within 10 percent. Household cups and spoons managed 29 percent within 25 percent. A review of physique sport recommends flexible eating and structured monitoring to lower mental health risk. Hand portions suit people who find weighing food stressful.

- Use palm, fist, cupped hand and thumb, and check once against a scale.

Tracking food · Beginner · Thin evidence · Sources: [Gibson 2016](https://doi.org/10.1017/jns.2016.22), [Helms 2019](https://doi.org/10.3390/sports7070172)

## Common mistakes

### Weighing cooked food but logging the raw entry

**Raw and cooked weights differ by the water gained or lost, so the entry must match the state you weighed.**

Rice, pasta and oats take up water when cooked and weigh more, while meat loses water and weighs less. A raw entry logged for cooked food (or the reverse) can be off by a large margin. Pick one habit: weigh raw before cooking, or choose a database entry that says cooked.

- Weigh food in the state the database entry names.
- Weigh dry foods before they cook when you can.

Tracking food · Beginner · Coaching practice

### Forgetting cooking oil and butter

**Fat has 9 kcal per gram, so a splash of oil in the pan can add a few hundred calories unseen.**

Fat provides 9 kcal per gram on the Atwater scale, so 10 g of oil adds about 90 kcal and a generous 25 g pour adds about 225. Oil is the classic missing entry in a log because it never sits on the plate as a measured item.

- Measure oil with a spoon or weigh the pan before and after.
- Log sauces and dressings the same way.

Tracking food · Beginner · Some support · Sources: [FAO 2003](https://www.fao.org/4/y5022e/y5022e04.htm)

### Eyeballing dense foods like nut butter, cheese and cereal

**Eyeballed portions of calorie-dense foods are easy to get wrong, and small errors there cost the most calories.**

In a study of 67 adults, estimates of pre-weighed foods using cups and spoons landed within 25 percent of the true weight only 29 percent of the time. The foods that hide energy, such as nut butter or granola, have the most calories per gram, so small errors cost more. Weigh these items, and eyeball vegetables if you like.

- Weigh the dense foods; estimate the low-calorie ones.

Tracking food · Beginner · Thin evidence · Sources: [Gibson 2016](https://doi.org/10.1017/jns.2016.22)

### Taking the first database entry without checking it

**App databases are good on average but hold wrong and duplicate entries that can swing a meal by hundreds of calories.**

A validation of MyFitnessPal in 50 participants found cleaned values matched a lab database well for energy (r=0.96), but 2.8 percent of entries had to be removed as implausible, using a 1,500 kcal per portion ceiling. A comparison of five apps found values for some nutrients, including protein and fat, lower than research software. Barcode scans are as good as the product record behind them.

- Compare the entry to the packet label.
- Prefer entries from the manufacturer, and delete odd ones.

Tracking food · Beginner · Some support · Sources: [Evenepoel 2020](https://doi.org/10.2196/18237), [Griffiths 2018](https://doi.org/10.1017/S1368980018000393)

### Not logging drinks, bites, tastes and sauces

**Small unlogged items are a large part of why logs read low.**

Under-reporting against doubly labeled water is common, but the reviews do not say which items go missing, so this is a practical reading and not a measured split. Milk in coffee, juice, snacks while cooking, and sauces add up across a week.

- Log as you go, not at the end of the day.
- Count liquid calories too.

Tracking food · Beginner · Thin evidence · Sources: [Burrows 2019](https://doi.org/10.3389/fendo.2019.00850)

### Logging a restaurant meal at the number on the menu

**Restaurant meals often hold more energy than stated, and the error is largest on individual items.**

Laboratory analysis of 269 foods from 42 restaurants found the average stated value was close, but 19 percent of items contained at least 100 kcal more than stated. In 29 reduced-energy restaurant foods, measured energy averaged 18 percent above stated, and free side dishes pushed it far higher. Non-chain restaurant meals averaged about 1,205 kcal. A generous estimate is safer than a hopeful one.

- Add 10 to 20 percent for restaurant meals when your goal is losing weight.

Tracking food · Beginner · Some support · Sources: [Urban 2011](https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2011.993), [Urban 2010](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jada.2009.10.003), [Urban 2016](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jand.2015.11.009)

### Tracking weekdays carefully and weekends loosely

**Weekend eating and activity can erase much of a weekday deficit.**

In 48 adults, weight rose on weekend days at baseline, and in the calorie-restriction group weight loss stopped on weekends. An analysis of 4,657 weights from 80 adults found weight higher on Sunday and Monday, decreasing through the week, which is normal and not by itself a sign of gain. People who compensated most were most likely to lose or maintain.

- Log the weekend with the same effort, or compare weekly averages.

Tracking food · Beginner · Some support · Sources: [Racette 2008](https://doi.org/10.1038/oby.2008.320), [Orsama 2014](https://doi.org/10.1159/000356147)

### Treating the tracker as exact, or quitting after one bad day

**Tracker numbers are estimates with real error, and a single high day changes little.**

Labels, databases, restaurant meals, wearables and your own memory all carry error, and wearable energy estimates vary widely with the activity. The log is useful for trends. A missed day or an over-target day matters little against weeks of data, and dropping the log altogether is the larger loss.

- Use a weekly average and adjust slowly.
- Restart the next meal, not the next Monday.

Tracking food · Intermediate · Thin evidence · Sources: [O’Driscoll 2020](https://doi.org/10.1136/bjsports-2018-099643), [Harvey 2019](https://doi.org/10.1002/oby.22382)

## Key numbers

| Number | What it is | Support | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.6-2.2 g per kg per day | Daily protein for lifters: The common target for building muscle: 0.7 to 1.0 g per lb a day. | Well supported | [Jäger 2017](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12970-017-0177-8), [Nunes 2022b](https://doi.org/10.1002/jcsm.12922), [Iraki 2019](https://doi.org/10.3390/sports7070154) |
| 0.25-0.55 g per kg per meal | Protein per serving: ISSN guide: 0.25 g per kg, or 20 to 40 g, a serving. A bodybuilding review suggests 0.40 to 0.55 g per kg per meal. | Some support | [Jäger 2017](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12970-017-0177-8), [Iraki 2019](https://doi.org/10.3390/sports7070154) |
| 4 · 4 · 9 · 7 kcal per g | Energy per gram of food: Protein 4, carbohydrate 4, fat 9 and alcohol 7 kcal per gram on food labels. | Rulebook | [FAO 2003](https://www.fao.org/4/y5022e/y5022e04.htm) |
| 10 % error band | Accuracy of the best equation: Mifflin-St Jeor was within 10 percent of measured resting rate for the most people. | Well supported | [Frankenfield 2005](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jada.2005.02.005) |
| 1.40-2.40 times resting rate | Activity multiplier range: Long-term sustainable activity levels for free-living adults, per FAO/WHO/UNU. | Rulebook | [FAO/WHO/UNU 2004](https://www.fao.org/4/y5686e/y5686e07.htm) |
| +20 % over the label | US label tolerance: A food is misbranded only above this; a typical snack runs a few percent over. | Rulebook | [UFDA 2023](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2023-title21-vol2/xml/CFR-2023-title21-vol2-sec101-9.xml), [Jumpertz 2013](https://doi.org/10.1002/oby.20185) |
| 19 % of true intake | Under-reporting in athletes: Self-reported energy intake was this much lower than measured expenditure. | Well supported | [Capling 2017](https://doi.org/10.3390/nu9121313) |
| 3-5 g per day | Creatine monohydrate dose: Daily dose from a physique-athlete review; lean-mass gain was about 1.1 kg with training. | Well supported | [Iraki 2019](https://doi.org/10.3390/sports7070154), [Delpino 2022](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.nut.2022.111791) |
| 3-6 mg per kg | Caffeine dose often studied: ISSN's 2010 stand: effective at about 3 to 6 mg per kg, no further gain at 9 or more. 5 mg/kg is 2.3 mg per lb. | Thin evidence | [Iraki 2019](https://doi.org/10.3390/sports7070154), [Grgic 2018](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12970-018-0216-0), [Goldstein 2010](https://doi.org/10.1186/1550-2783-7-5) |
| 25-29 g per day | Fibre target: Intake at which health benefits were greatest in pooled studies. | Well supported | [Reynolds 2019](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(18)31809-9) |

## Protein targets by goal and body weight

Daily protein in g per kg and per lb, with worked examples for 70 kg (154 lb) and 90 kg (198 lb) people.

| Goal | g per kg | g per lb | 70 kg (154 lb) | 90 kg (198 lb) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Maintain or build muscle (ISSN, sufficient) | 1.4-2.0 | 0.64-0.91 | 98-140 g | 126-180 g |
| Build muscle (common target) | 1.6-2.2 | 0.73-1.00 | 112-154 g | 144-198 g |
| Physique athlete in contest prep | 1.8-2.7 | 0.82-1.22 | 126-189 g | 162-243 g |
| Lean lifter in a calorie deficit | 2.3-3.1 | 1.04-1.41 | 161-217 g | 207-279 g |
| One serving (ISSN guide) | 0.25 | 0.11 | about 18 g | about 23 g |
| One serving (off-season review) | 0.40-0.55 | 0.18-0.25 | 28-39 g | 36-50 g |

Some support · Sources: [Jäger 2017](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12970-017-0177-8), [Roberts 2020](https://doi.org/10.2478/hukin-2019-0096), [Iraki 2019](https://doi.org/10.3390/sports7070154)

## Hand-portion guide

A rough guide for estimating a serving with your own hand when you do not weigh food. Check it against a scale once.

| Food group | Hand measure | Rough yield |
|---|---|---|
| Protein foods (meat, fish, tofu) | Palm, same thickness | About 20-30 g protein |
| Starchy carbohydrate (rice, pasta, potato) | Cupped hand, cooked | About 25-35 g carbohydrate |
| Vegetables and salad | Fist | About 1 cup, low in energy |
| Fats (oil, butter, nut butter) | Thumb | About 7-12 g fat |
| Dense snacks (nuts, cheese) | Thumb of cheese, small handful of nuts | Wide range: weigh these when you can |

Coaching practice · Sources: [Gibson 2016](https://doi.org/10.1017/jns.2016.22)

## Supplement evidence at a glance

How the common supplements rate for people who lift, from strongest to weakest evidence.

| Supplement | Evidence | What it does | Typical dose |
|---|---|---|---|
| Creatine monohydrate | Strong | Adds lean mass and strength with training | 3-5 g a day |
| Caffeine | Strong | Small gain in strength and power | About 3-6 mg/kg |
| Protein powder | Strong as a convenience | Helps meet daily protein, no special magic | 20-40 g per serving |
| Beta-alanine | Moderate | Helps efforts lasting 1 to 4 minutes | 4-6 g a day for 2+ weeks, in split doses |
| Citrulline malate | Limited | About 3 extra reps per exercise in trials | 6-8 g, 40-60 min before |
| BCAA pills | Weak | No human data on oral BCAA alone for muscle | Not needed with enough protein |
| Testosterone boosters | Poor | No testosterone data for most ingredients | Avoid |

Some support · Sources: [Kreider 2017](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12970-017-0173-z), [Delpino 2022](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.nut.2022.111791), [Grgic 2018](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12970-018-0216-0), [Jäger 2017](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12970-017-0177-8), [Trexler 2015](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12970-015-0090-y), [Vårvik 2021](https://doi.org/10.1123/ijsnem.2020-0295), [Wolfe 2017](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12970-017-0184-9), [Clemesha 2020](https://doi.org/10.5534/wjmh.190043), [Maughan 2018](https://doi.org/10.1136/bjsports-2018-099027), [Goldstein 2010](https://doi.org/10.1186/1550-2783-7-5)

## Terms

- **Atwater factors**: Standard energy values per gram that food labels use: 4 kcal for protein and carbohydrate, 9 for fat, 7 for alcohol. They are averages, not measurements of your food.
- **Ergogenic aid**: Something taken to improve exercise performance or training results. Creatine and caffeine are the best-supported examples.
- **Kilojoule (kJ) and kilocalorie (kcal)**: Two units of food energy. One kcal, the calorie on most labels, equals 4.184 kJ. Many countries print kJ.
- **Leucine**: An essential amino acid that acts as a trigger for muscle protein synthesis. Animal proteins contain more than most plant proteins, per gram of protein.
- **Macronutrients (macros)**: The three nutrients that provide most energy: protein, carbohydrate and fat. Alcohol is sometimes counted as a fourth source of energy.
- **Maintenance calories**: The daily energy intake at which your body weight stays steady over weeks. Also called total daily energy expenditure.
- **Resting metabolic rate (RMR)**: The energy your body uses at rest to keep you alive, usually 60 to 70 percent of a day for inactive people, estimated by equations or measured.
- **Thermic effect of food (TEF)**: The energy used to digest, absorb and store food, about 5 to 15 percent of daily energy expenditure on a mixed diet, and higher with protein and alcohol.
